policy_name: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (NIST AI 100-1)
issuing_authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
regulatory_regime: Voluntary U.S. federal AI risk management guidance (National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 mandate)
geo_constraints: None; voluntary framework intended for any organization designing, developing, deploying or using AI systems

key_dates.event: AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1) released, with companion AI RMF Playbook
Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) published as a cross-sectoral profile of the AI RMF

White House 'America's AI Action Plan' directs NIST to revise the AI RMF (incl. removing references to misinformation, DEI and climate change); NIST page states revision underway, no draft published as of Nov 2026

covered_entities: AI actors across the AI lifecycle (designers, developers, deployers, operators, evaluators, users) in any organization
covered_systems: AI systems (engineered or machine-based systems that generate outputs such as predictions, recommendations or decisions)
conditions: Voluntary; organizations select and tailor outcomes (subcategories) based on context, risk tolerance and resources
objective: Provide a voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific framework to help organizations manage AI risks and promote trustworthy and responsible development and use of AI systems, structured around the GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE functions.
conflict_rule: Voluntary and non-binding; does not supersede applicable law. GOVERN 1.1 expects legal and regulatory requirements to be understood and managed, so binding law prevails.

sources_consulted: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ddps007/daaa (text extraction of NIST.AI.100-1.pdf used to verify wording)
record_provenance.notes: nist.gov / nvlpubs.nist.gov / airc.nist.gov could not be fetched from this session (network policy). Clause wording was verified against a plain-text extraction of the official NIST.AI.100-1.pdf hosted on Hugging Face (third-party mirror) and is consistent with NIST-domain search excerpts; re-check against the NIST PDF. 'America's AI Action Plan' (July 2025) directed NIST to revise the AI RMF; secondary sources and NIST's page (per search results) indicate a revision is underway but as of Nov 2026 no new version has been published, so AI RMF 1.0 remains current. Exact July 2025 date of the Action Plan taken from general knowledge (23 July 2025) and not re-verified here.

clauses.original_text: GOVERN 1.1: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
clauses.object: legal and regulatory requirements involving AI
clauses.requirement: identify, manage and document applicable AI legal and regulatory requirements
clauses.purpose: legal compliance as a foundation of AI risk governance
clauses.interpretation_notes: Framework outcomes are phrased as states ('are understood') rather than imperatives; modality SHOULD reflects the voluntary nature.

clauses.original_text: GOVERN 4.1: Organizational policies and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize potential negative impacts.
clauses.action: put in place policies and practices
clauses.requirement: establish policies fostering a safety-first mindset across the AI lifecycle
clauses.purpose: minimize potential negative impacts of AI systems
clauses.affected_asset: people and organizations affected by AI systems
clauses.interpretation_notes: Cultural/organizational outcome; measurable evidence is left to the Playbook's suggested actions.

clauses.original_text: GOVERN 6.1: Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of a third-party’s intellectual property or other rights.
clauses.object: AI risks from third-party entities (software, data, supply chain)
clauses.requirement: address third-party and supply-chain AI risks, including IP infringement
clauses.purpose: manage supply-chain and third-party rights risks
clauses.affected_asset: third-party intellectual property and other rights; organizational systems
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems using third-party software, data or models
clauses.interpretation_notes: Verbatim from Table 1; GOVERN 6.2 (contingency processes for third-party failures) is the companion outcome.

clauses.original_text: MEASURE 2.6: The AI system is evaluated regularly for safety risks – as identified in the MAP function. The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be safe, its residual negative risk does not exceed the risk tolerance, and it can fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits. Safety metrics reflect system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures.
clauses.requirement: regularly evaluate safety; demonstrate residual risk within tolerance and safe failure before deployment
clauses.condition: before deployment and on a regular basis thereafter
clauses.purpose: ensure AI systems are safe and fail safely
clauses.affected_asset: human life, health, property and the environment
clauses.applicable_systems: any AI system to be deployed
clauses.interpretation_notes: Combines a recurring evaluation outcome with a pre-deployment demonstration; 'risk tolerance' is organization-defined (GOVERN 1.3).

clauses.original_text: MANAGE 1.1: A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.
clauses.requirement: make a documented go/no-go decision based on whether the system meets its intended purpose
clauses.condition: based on outputs of the MAP and MEASURE functions
clauses.purpose: avoid developing or deploying systems that do not meet objectives or carry unacceptable risk
clauses.interpretation_notes: Commonly read as the framework's explicit go/no-go gate.

clauses.original_text: MANAGE 2.4: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
clauses.action: establish mechanisms and assign responsibility to supersede, disengage or deactivate
clauses.object: AI systems behaving inconsistently with intended use
clauses.requirement: maintain working shutdown/override mechanisms with assigned owners
clauses.condition: when performance or outcomes are inconsistent with intended use
clauses.purpose: contain harm from malfunctioning or misused AI
clauses.interpretation_notes: Often called the 'kill switch' subcategory in secondary literature.
